    1. GitHub Copilot training

    Learn GitHub Copilot in VS Code

    GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code (VS Code) works on the files on your computer. You ask in plain words, and it reads your documents, writes new files and runs commands. It asks you before it runs a command that could change something. You can undo the edits it makes to your files.

    These trainings teach you to direct it. You don't need to write code. Start with Getting started; each training builds on the one before it.

    The trainings

    • BeginnerGetting started

      Make your first request, change Copilot's work and undo it, have it explain code, and give it instructions for a folder.

      4 units · about 25 minutes

      Not started

    • IntermediateSkills

      Save your instructions for a task you repeat, so Copilot follows them when you ask for that task.

      2 units · about 15 minutes

      Not started

    • AdvancedCustom agents

      Set Copilot up for one role, such as reviewer or planner, with its own instructions and tools.

      3 units · about 25 minutes

      Not started

    • IntermediateConnecting your tools

      Connect Copilot to another service, such as GitHub, so Copilot can get information from that service.

      1 unit · about 15 minutes

      Not started

    Which to use when

    Most of the time, you just ask. When you keep repeating yourself, or Copilot needs something it doesn't have, you can set Copilot up ahead of time. Find your case below, and try the smallest option that covers it.

    When this happensUseTaught in
    You need something just this onceJust the requestGetting started
    You give the same rules in every request in a folderCustom instructionsGetting started
    You explain a task, such as a weekly summary, step by step every timeA skillSkills
    You describe the same role, such as reviewer or planner, chat after chatA custom agentCustom agents
    Copilot needs information from another service, such as GitHubA connectionConnecting your tools

    Often more than one would work, and one job can use several. VS Code has other ways to set Copilot up, such as hooks and prompt files. These trainings don't cover them.

    When you need it

    • Help: what to do when something goes wrong, what to ask Copilot when you're stuck, and common questions.
    • Glossary: the words these trainings use.
